column2: req_desc

Plate lookup.
Entering a plate normalises it to the country's published format, rejects an invalid one with no registry request, and otherwise reads the registry and shows the donor or the published not-found or not-catalogued result, with only the latest lookup able to change anything on screen.

Hand-entered frame details.
A rider can enter frame details by hand and try the fit, and the result is always marked unconfirmed.

Feeler Sweep rail drive.
Selecting the pack or hub flies it out along its assembly axis, fades the blocking panels, and lets drag or arrow keys drive it along its rail while the Clearance readout publishes travel and station gaps and the rail handle stays on the part's projected leading edge.

First contact.
The part stops at the published travel of the first station it cannot pass, the fouling edge turns accent red in the pixels at its published screen position, and the readout names the fouling feature.

Release and full seat.
Releasing a drag short of contact, or a cancelled touch, springs the part back to the rail start, and reaching full seat or first contact runs the server fit check.

Readout agrees with verdict.
The verdict word and millimetre figures from the server appear beside a readout showing the same figures.

Pack clearance stations.
The server decides pack clearance on stored tenths of a millimetre at the three stations of the frame revision that the first-admission year selects, with the published minimum itself passing.

Hub and shaft checks.
Hub width is checked against the swingarm and shaft length against the sprocket line under the same minimum.

Axle split.
The front axle share is computed from part masses and positions and must stay within the published limit of the donor's share, with the limit itself passing.

Mass, dimensions and tank.
A build fails if it exceeds registered mass or grows overall dimensions, and every kit quote carries the required fuel tank removal line.

Road class and power.
Kit power is checked against the published limit for the target road class and against the donor-relative limit.

Class move costs and notices.
Moving up a class adds a VAT-free inspection fee line and the plate, helmet and licence notices.

Figures update in place.
Changing pack, hub, class, units, fulfilment or country updates clearance, range, VAT and schedule without a reload, marks figures checking or not current until the server answers, drops superseded replies, and announces the result.

Units never change a verdict.
Switching between millimetres and inches or kilograms and pounds changes display only and never a verdict.

Address holds the configuration.
The configurator address holds donor, pack, hub, class, units, fulfilment and country, so reload, share, back and forward restore them.

Place of supply VAT.
VAT is extracted per line in integer cents at the delivery country's rate for posted kits and the Dutch rate for workshop fitting.

Pinned teardown story.
Scrolling the pinned story maps progress to a published stage for each part, monotonic in both directions, so scrolling back reassembles the moped exactly, in pixels as well as attributes.

Scene keyboard and parts list.
The scene is one Tab stop with the published orbit, zoom, reset and exit keys, and a DOM parts list with roving focus mirrors every 3D part and selects it in the scene.

Touch gestures.
On touch, a horizontal drag orbits, a vertical swipe scrolls the page, a pinch zooms, the first movement locks the axis until lift, and rail drag works only on the selected part's handle.

Deposit gate.
A kit deposit is taken only for a registry-confirmed donor whose current fit verdict passes, whose registration still matches a fresh read, and whose quote is still current.

Keyboard checkout.
A rider can complete the whole configurator-to-deposit flow using only the keyboard at every published viewport, with focus held inside the checkout dialog and returned to its opener.

Deposit landing.
Paying a deposit lands on that order's own page, which shows the same screen when reloaded or opened directly.

One transaction per key.
A money request carrying one idempotency key makes one Kill Bill transaction across double clicks, retries and shop instances sharing the database, with the published replay and conflict answers.

Callback registration.
The shop registers one secret callback per instance URL on its Kill Bill tenant, retrying until Kill Bill answers.

Notification belief.
A notification moves an order only when its secret path matches and a re-read of the payment from Kill Bill agrees.

Repeats and reordering.
Repeated, concurrent and out-of-order deliveries, on one instance or across instances, including Kill Bill's timed retries, produce the correct final state, one state change and no second mail.

Pending until confirmed.
A payment reads pending until a believed notification marks it paid, however long that takes.

Receipt once.
Each confirmed payment sends one VAT receipt, only after confirmation, even when two shop instances handle the same delivery.

Payment schedule.
A deposit and three instalments sum exactly to the order total under the published rounding and leftover rule.

Cent allocation.
Each payment is split across lines and VAT by the published rule so parts sum exactly to each payment, each line and the total.

Paying by stage.
A rider pays stages in order, and paying out of order, repeating a paid stage, or paying while another payment or a refund is in flight is refused as published.

Plan panel survives ticks.
The open plan panel keeps its open state, focus and typed entries through status polling and the hold countdown, and a stale save is refused.

Monthly collection.
Instalments fall due monthly, anchored on the deposit's confirmation date in Amsterdam business time, and the server collects them without a client.

Retries, arrears and deferral.
A failed collection retries on the published schedule, then moves the order into arrears, paying the overdue stage returns it to running, and a collection falling due during a pending refund is deferred without counting an attempt.

Order transitions.
Order states move only along the published machine, and every illegal move gets its published rejection.

Withdrawal.
A rider may withdraw before fitting and before inspection passed, and for a delivered posted kit until the rolled-forward deadline judged by the server, with collected money refunded through Kill Bill.

Partial refund.
A fitter's partial refund targets one line, draws from the latest payment first, cannot exceed what the line has collected even across parallel refunds, is refused while a stage is pending, and reverses VAT cent-exact.

Balance re-spread.
A refund that returned money re-spreads the unpaid balance across the remaining instalments under the published rule, using only the returned draws.

Each draw believed separately.
A refund reads pending until Kill Bill has settled every draw, then returned, partly returned or failed, and the order's flag and one credit note for the returned amount follow only after that.

Bike comparison.
Built e-mopeds can be filtered by road class and compared by range in place, with the filter held in the address.

Last slot and one hold.
Of any number of simultaneous claims on a test-ride slot, on any shop instance, exactly one holds it and the rest are told it has gone, and a rider has at most one live hold.

Server clock hold.
A test-ride hold expires on the server's clock and frees its slot with no client involved, whatever the device clock says, and instances sharing the database expire it once.

Ride confirmation.
Confirming a live hold lands on the ride's own page and sends one confirmation mail.

Booking and cancellation cutoffs.
The same-day booking and free cancellation cutoffs are judged by the server in Amsterdam business time, with the true offset on the slot's date.

Test-ride days.
The fitter opens slots for a bike and date, sees the day's rides, and marks confirmed rides ridden or no-show, while polling keeps typed entries and focus.

Payments desk.
The fitter sees each payment, refund and draw with its provider-confirmed status and can issue line refunds from the order's desk page, while polling keeps typed entries, selection, focus and the last message.

Accounts and sign-in landing.
Riders can register and sign in, each role lands on its published route, and a session is shared by every instance on the database.

Own orders and rides only.
A rider can open only their own orders and rides, and another rider's address gives the same not-found answer as a missing one.

Published empty lists.
Each empty order, ride and desk list shows its published wording character for character.

Kill Bill paused.
With Kill Bill down, shopping keeps working, money controls are disabled but stay focusable, the published banner shows and pending never reads as paid.

Registry unreachable.
With the registry down, the published banner shows, hand entry and fit trials work, and a kit deposit stays blocked.

Boot and recover.
The shop boots with either provider down and recovers without a restart or a reload when the provider returns, including re-reading an open plate address, within the limit stated in Feedback states.

Run manifest and health.
The app starts from the run manifest on the published port and answers the health route with either provider down.

Server boundary.
The server enforces same-origin requests and body limits, and it never serves source files or credentials.

Published layouts.
The scene, parts panel and price rail rearrange at exactly the published breakpoints with no horizontal overflow, including live resize with a panel open.

Closed panels unavailable.
A closed parts sheet or navigation drawer is hidden and cannot be reached by Tab or activated at any viewport, and focus never lands on a hidden control.

Motion and reduced motion.
Every published motion has its stated timing, numbers on screen are never hidden by animation, and the reduced-motion substitute keeps every function and applies to an open page within the published limit.

Still drawing without WebGL.
Without WebGL, a still drawing generated from the same parts table replaces the canvas, with the same slider and figures and a visible fouling edge.

Drawing sheet look.
The product reads as a flat, ruled engineering drawing sheet with a recognisable procedural moped, dimension lines on parts, and a status word beside every money figure.

Provider wiring in source.
The source builds the moped procedurally from one parts table, and it reads every provider credential from the environment and calls the real providers.

Switch to workshop fitting.
A posted kit may switch to workshop fitting after the deposit, only with no money in flight and no refund ever returned, making no Kill Bill transaction and leaving confirmed stage amounts unchanged.

VAT correction on a switch.
A switch recomputes confirmed VAT cent-exact at the new rate, re-spreads the unpaid balance, and sends one VAT correction mail only when the correction is not zero.

Inspection confirmed by the registry.
A class-move order reaches inspection passed only after a fresh registry read shows the new class and plate colour, with one inspection mail.

Spent inspection fee.
Once inspection has passed, the inspection fee cannot be refunded and the order cannot be withdrawn.

Dated fee and changed donor.
A quote uses the inspection fee in force on the shop's Amsterdam date, a stale quoted order is re-quoted with no Kill Bill call before any deposit, and a differing total at order creation is refused.

Session ends mid-task.
A session ending mid-task opens a sign-in dialog over the page on the next action, keeps all input, retries a plan save once, and never re-sends a money action without a fresh press.

Both rails driven before checkout.
Checkout on a kit stays closed until both rails have been driven to their stops in this page view for the current donor, pack, hub and class.
/app/run.json exists with string install, build, serve and "_schema":"run-manifest-v1".

THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md at the repository root lists every shipped package and bundled font with its licence, where shipped packages means the production dependency tree (npm ls --omit=dev --all --json).
Shipped packages and fonts use only MIT, BSD, ISC, Apache-2.0 or SIL Open Font licences.
No datastore, queue or provider beyond PostgreSQL, Kill Bill, Mailpit and WireMock is added.
Seeded provider configuration, including the compose files and the WireMock baseline mappings, is left unchanged.
All fonts, scripts and assets are served from the app, with no runtime request to any other origin.
